items.title: New markets
items.note: One director named it as his top catalog wish, and Brittany said a senior PM already owns international scaling. Real priority, with an existing owner. Frame the vision page as partnering with that work. The DoorDash angle is my inference from the news and nobody said it.

quotes.quote: as we start to look to go international, um, the ability to do international means we need a lot more attributes and things like that into the catalog.
quotes.context: Mike asked what is on his wish list for catalog.

quotes.quote: we need to be able to have, you know, additional tax information coming through. Other times, just, yeah, the international data formats are different.
quotes.context: Same answer.

quotes.quote: a lot of the needs of international expansion are pretty high on the list of things that I'm looking for in the catalog stuff.
quotes.context: Same answer.

quotes.quote: today, um, we have a senior PM who is responsible for how do we take what we do in North America and scale it internationally to different languages, different markets.
quotes.context: Describing the current team. Means an owner for international already exists.

items.title: Legacy system
items.note: Three people: Brittany, Peggy and Sonali. Ten-year-old architecture, legacy code tied to incidents, and an open rebuild question.

quotes.quote: Instacart to make it easy decides to partner with point of sale. To get the point of sale data and then backwards construct a catalog out of the point of sale
quotes.context: Mike asked whether diagnostics and explainability were a pain point. Speaker labeled 'Them' in the transcript; the section is Brittany's jam, so attribution is Brittany.

quotes.quote: It has 10 years of legacy code that we're fighting with, right, because of which we have incidents.
quotes.context: Mike asked what was most broken from a software engineering perspective.

quotes.quote: We don't want to touch it because it's, like, there's legacy systems. It's a huge project, whatever, whatever.
quotes.context: Mike asked what she looks for in a PM partner; she named knowing when to re-architect from first principles.

quotes.quote: because we've been around for so long, we, like, are, like, stuck with these systems, right? But when are the right times to re-architect or evolve, right?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: let's stress test the current framework to see if it enables us to scale.
quotes.context: Mike asked whether a rebuild is likely in 2027. She said the proposal belongs to the PM, EM, and ops manager.

quotes.quote: we don't shy away from big projects, rebuilds if there's strong conviction that it's the right thing to do.
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: should we actually be going and rebuilding the way that we store and generate attribute information?
quotes.context: Mike asked about big projects for the first six months.

quotes.quote: simple things like we were literally, I feel like, three, four months apart, have the same issue bubble up as a different incident.
quotes.context: Mike asked what was most broken.

quotes.quote: A lot of that actually meant something about the way we have architected our solution had to change. You can't symptomatically just fix it, right?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: getting really crisp on the ownership and getting all of those runbooks in order
quotes.context: Same answer, the second half of the fix.

quotes.quote: But I feel like enough investment hasn't been made.
quotes.context: Same answer, opening.

items.title: Attribute launch effort
items.note: Tarang described the per-attribute steps and said the process needs rethinking. Brittany called it time-consuming and error-prone. Nobody said "hand-built" and a self-serve platform exists (GenCon, grown out of PARSE), so the softened wording is right. Nobody mentioned a standard intake spec either way.

quotes.quote: if we had to solve for actually everything that consumers of catalog are hoping to get from catalog over the next couple of years, they just need a lot more catalog data.
quotes.context: Mike asked which roadmap projects he was excited about. Labeled 'Them'; section header confirms Tarang.

quotes.quote: the ways we have come up with how we even generate new attributes has to probably be, like, completely rethought.
quotes.context: Same answer.

quotes.quote: All the way from product definition to the process of then, like, coming up with a pipeline structure, then running the pipelines, and then, like, actually doing it at scale with the quality bar.
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: someone who understands data as a product and, and how that will scale with, like, agentic shopping, with these downstream teams wanting more and more data attributes.
quotes.context: Mike asked what Brittany is looking for in this hire.

quotes.quote: We're always trying to deliver more data to these downstream teams, like search, replacements, etc.
quotes.context: What she looks for in a PM partner.

quotes.quote: And the way that this process works today is time-consuming and also prone to human error.
quotes.context: Mike asked about the first six months and the two-year outlook.

quotes.quote: I will then create the right audit steps. I'll maybe use testing using LLM as a judge, and then maybe I'll also send some stuff off to a BPO to then manually label, where I'm not sure.
quotes.context: Describing how Peggy's team builds the gluten-free pipeline. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: And now, for them to do that, they need the right tooling and platform, right?
quotes.context: Same description, continued.

quotes.quote: a really good PM partner balances those business needs with also the enablement or foundation needs as well because to build faster, we also have to invest in the tooling and how do we balance both those things.
quotes.context: Mike asked what she looks for in a PM partner.

quotes.quote: how do we actually support and build tools that our operations team can use to create that new information
quotes.context: Describing the role. A charter statement more than a complaint, so a soft confirmation.

items.title: Ground truth
items.strength: Moderate on the problem, weak on "no golden sets"
items.note: Tarang said there is no ground truth to ingest for generated tags, and the bar is 99 to 99.5 percent precision. Nobody said golden sets are missing. LLM-as-judge and BPO labeling are in use, a PM owns ground truth quality, and the JD asks for golden set audit experience. Golden sets may well exist, which is why the page says create or solidify.

quotes.quote: All those tags, we actually generate them ourselves. ... there's no ground truth data that we can just ingest to make that happen.
quotes.context: Describing the Generated Content team. Labeled 'Them'; an em-dash stutter elided.

quotes.quote: how would you think through, like, where to get that data from, right? Internal versus external.
quotes.context: Posed as a case question about building a GLP-1 attribute, so it signals the problem without describing current state.

quotes.quote: what underlying data does it need for them to be able to hit a 99% precision and recall bar for that new data.
quotes.context: Describing the role.

quotes.quote: Especially looking at allergens you're trying to hit 99.5% precision.
quotes.context: Questioning Mike's source selection logic. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: especially for health, especially for, like, allergens, like, we cannot get tagging something tree nut free wrong.
quotes.context: Roadmap excitement question. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: Um, they also think about general, like, ground truth catalog quality.
quotes.context: Same PM as above. Means someone already owns ground truth quality, so golden sets may exist.

quotes.quote: Familiarity with data pipelines, ML extraction workflows, or quality evaluation frameworks such as golden set audits, human-in-the-loop review, or precision/recall measurement.
quotes.context: Listed as a preferred qualification. Shows the team values golden set audits; it does not say whether they exist.

quotes.quote: I will then create the right audit steps. I'll maybe use testing using LLM as a judge, and then maybe I'll also send some stuff off to a BPO to then manually label, where I'm not sure.
quotes.context: Describing how Peggy's team builds the gluten-free pipeline. Labeled 'Them'.

items.title: Opaque precedence
items.note: Brittany and Peggy both described it, including retailer contracts that change precedence and retailers asking why a value shows.

quotes.quote: It's absolutely a pain point. We have and I think the catalog was built 10 years ago.
quotes.context: Mike asked whether diagnostics and explainability were a pain point for ops. Labeled 'Them'; section confirms Brittany.

quotes.quote: Very much so. We, we face the same issue.
quotes.context: Mike asked the same diagnostics question.

quotes.quote: there's general confusion because, like, it's not linear across attributes and it's not linear across retailers.
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: even sometimes between marketplace and SFP for a particular retailer, it can be different. So that adds to the confusion.
quotes.context: Same answer. SFP is Storefront Pro, the white-label product.

quotes.quote: we have some, like, contractual obligations, right, with retailers where we, like, maybe promote more of their data, but that's not the same for, like, retailer B, right?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: I think documentation varies.
quotes.context: Mike asked about documentation quality.

quotes.quote: So one of the challenges that we have within the catalog space is how do you actually make sure that when you have data from all of these different sources, you're making fast decisions on what's actually accurate at that given point of time.
quotes.context: Mike asked where catalog data comes from.

quotes.quote: different sources, how would you determine what's the right source? Especially looking at allergens you're trying to hit 99.5% precision.
quotes.context: Questioning Mike's proposed verification layer. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: we have varying data inputs from different sources at different quality levels. How might we, like, detect issues at scale and also fix them at scale
quotes.context: Overview of the catalog ops team.

quotes.quote: Sometimes retailers will come to us and, like, oh, I never sent this in my file. Why is it XYZ, right?
quotes.context: Diagnostics and explainability discussion.

quotes.quote: how might you explain it back to the, I don't know, retailer, right?
quotes.context: Mike asked about documentation; she said internal tooling improved but retailer explanation lags.

quotes.quote: a PM who's focused on our enterprise relationships and how we work specifically with retailers to manage their catalogs and allow for bidirectional feedback with them so that we're sharing errors
quotes.context: Describing the PM team. Stated as a charter, which implies the gap.

items.title: Unclear meaning of some attributes
items.note: Downstream teams cannot tell what fields mean or whether to trust them. Peggy called a semantic layer her 2027 ask. Agents need attributes modeled differently from product page badges.

quotes.quote: we don't do a great job of this today on how we might build a better semantic layer for all of our downstream teams
quotes.context: Mike asked about the biggest technology opportunity for 2027.

quotes.quote: there's lots of, like, data fields, a lot of, like, attributes, and they don't know what is this data? Should I use it or should I not use it?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: What's the quality? What is the freshness?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: maybe one of the challenges is that they are just using the attributes that we deliver incorrectly 'cause they just don't know how they're supposed to.
quotes.context: Mike asked what a semantic layer looks like to her.

quotes.quote: any attribute we create now becomes a badge on the product detail page. And that's what an attribute is.
quotes.context: Explaining pain points after Mike asked about diagnostics. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: what an attribute means for agentic shopping is very different than what an attribute means for what's shown on a PDP page.
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: Partner called Clementine as well as integrations with OpenAI and starting to see how is that the same and different from how they shop Instacart. And what data needs are there?
quotes.context: Mike asked about the 12-month outlook for the catalog PM.

quotes.quote: in the world of AI, it's going to force us to rethink ... the underlying infrastructure and data structure for how we store that information.
quotes.context: Describing the first six months of the role.

quotes.quote: Now with agentic shopping, we have this Clementine, which is a kind of internal agentic shopping experience, which equates to more data needs.
quotes.context: What she looks for in a PM partner.

quotes.quote: do we have to do that with the changing needs of our data and, like, AI and agentic?
quotes.context: On when to re-architect.

quotes.quote: we need to understand better the challenges that downstream teams have with it today.
quotes.context: Mike asked whether a rebuild is likely in 2027. Filler and a stutter removed.

quotes.quote: don't wanna, like, commit to that before we actually understand the downstream use cases.
quotes.context: Answering the semantic layer question. Stutter removed.

quotes.quote: we also want to understand how they're using the data. Some is more explicit and some is more implicit, but I think that also shapes how we build.
quotes.context: Mike asked about catalog's role in surfacing a GLP-1 attribute.

items.title: Pipeline decay
items.note: Peggy on refreshes, audits and monitoring. Sonali and Tarang on incidents that recur because fixes stay short-term.

quotes.quote: data has to get refreshed, right? We might have to do ongoing audits or monitor the quality of all our AI pipelines.
quotes.context: What she looks for in a PM partner.

quotes.quote: If we just continue to build the new, then we'll continue to get escalations on the stuff we've already shipped and maintained. And catalog being a data product means that maintenance is always top of mind.
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: her team creates now hundreds of these pipelines.
quotes.context: Describing Peggy's team. Labeled 'Them'.

quotes.quote: simple things like we were literally, I feel like, three, four months apart, have the same issue bubble up as a different incident.
quotes.context: Mike asked what was most broken.

quotes.quote: A lot of that actually meant something about the way we have architected our solution had to change. You can't symptomatically just fix it, right?
quotes.context: Same answer, continued.

quotes.quote: getting really crisp on the ownership and getting all of those runbooks in order
quotes.context: Same answer, the second half of the fix.
